notes: L0 accepts only horizontal or vertical walls and rejects proper X crossings BEFORE any change (§E.5). Every case here must leave the canonical model identical (modelUnchanged).

cases.description: Add a vertical wall that crosses the middle of a horizontal wall (proper X crossing).
arithmetic: New wall x = 2000 for y in [-1000, 1000]; w1 is y = 0 for x in [0, 4000].
Intersection (2000, 0): 0 < 2000 < 4000 (interior of w1) and -1000 < 0 < 1000 (interior of the new wall) -> proper X crossing -> rejected in L0.
dx = 3000, dy = 1000: both non-zero -> neither horizontal nor vertical -> rejected.

cases.description: Add a wall that is off by only 1 mm from horizontal. The model never 'fixes' it silently; making it straight is the job of snapping before the command (PH2-T03).
arithmetic: dx = 3000, dy = 1: dy != 0 and dx != 0 -> not axis-aligned -> rejected (I4 in L0).

cases.description: Drag a junction so its wall would cross another wall (E.13: 'dragging a junction across another wall').
arithmetic: After the move w2 would run x = 2000, y from -1000 to 3000. It contains (2000, 0) in its interior (-1000 < 0 < 3000), which is also interior to w1 (0 < 2000 < 4000) -> X crossing -> rejected, j3 stays at (2000, 1000).

cases.description: Move one end junction so its wall becomes diagonal.
arithmetic: w1 would go from (0,0) to (4000,500): dx = 4000, dy = 500 -> not axis-aligned -> rejected.
